quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [A Skeptical Look at Productivity Hacks] Every year brings a new productivity method promising to transform how people work, from rigid time-blocking schedules to apps that gamify to-do lists. Few of these approaches are studied rigorously before becoming popular, and fewer still are followed up years later to see whether their early adopters actually sustained the habit, let alone became more productive because of it.
quests.question: What is the writer most skeptical about, according to the passage?
options: Whether people should use to-do lists at all
Whether apps really beat old paper planners
Whether popular methods are proven effective over time
Whether time-blocking is even considered a real method
quests.correctAnswer: Whether popular methods are proven effective over time
quests.hint: Notice the writer's focus on a lack of rigorous study and long-term follow-up.
quests.explanation: The writer questions the lack of rigorous study and long-term evidence behind popular productivity trends.

quests.explanation: Despite similar or greater housing approvals in Brookline, planners point to weaker transit access as the key difference.
